page: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong computational and memory capabilities. The Intel Xeon processor achieves top-tier performance in single-core Geekbench tests, software compilation, and image processing. Multi-core performance is also strong, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated matrix operations. Memory read bandwidth is highly efficient, scoring in the top 25% for both cached small-block and uncached large-block reads, though large-block write bandwidth remains in the average tier.

The absence of local NVMe storage requires workloads to rely entirely on network-attached storage, which may limit performance for IOPS-heavy local database operations despite a strong baseline network speed of 15 Gbps. However, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and strong memory bandwidth make this server highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive applications without the overhead of local storage. It is well-suited for large-scale in-memory databases like Redis, high-throughput static web serving, software compilation, and CPU-based LLM inference tasks.
description: The Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.16xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server featuring 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. It is configured with 512.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core, but lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, the server delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps. Benchmarks indicate top-tier single-core performance, excellent static web serving throughput, and strong multi-core processing capabilities, aided by Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. While large-block memory write performance is average, its massive memory capacity and high read bandwidth make it highly efficient for memory-intensive workloads. It is optimized for in-memory databases, software compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
